Symmetry & Geometry

Laws, Breaking, and Brains

Geometry is the stage; symmetry is the rulebook. Order emerges when symmetries hold — and structure emerges when they break.

  • Geometry is physics in disguise: many laws are geometric statements.
  • Symmetry organises reality: conserved quantities and selection rules follow from invariances.
  • Structure arises by breaking those symmetries — from the Higgs field to biological patterning.
  • Brains are symmetry engines: they detect invariances and use them for rapid, energy‑efficient generalisation.

Physical Laws in Geometric Form

  • Spacetime geometry (Riemannian/Lorentzian manifolds) encodes gravity as curvature (Einstein).
  • Gauge geometry encodes forces as curvature of internal bundles (U(1), SU(2), SU(3)).
  • Lorentz symmetry unifies space & time; invariant speed of light.

Noether’s Theorem — Symmetry → Conservation

  • Time translation symmetry ⇒ energy conservation.
  • Space translation symmetry ⇒ momentum conservation.
  • Rotation symmetry ⇒ angular momentum conservation.
  • Generalised to gauge symmetries (charge conservation).

Symmetry

Conservation law

Noether (1918)

Symmetry Breaking → Structure

  • Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB): equations symmetric, solutions asymmetric.
  • Higgs mechanism: electroweak SU(2)×U(1) → U(1); W/Z gain mass, photon stays massless.
  • Goldstone modes from broken continuous symmetries (become massive via Higgs in gauge theories).
  • Biology: bilateral body plans with left–right asymmetry; Turing patterns in morphogenesis.

Brains Exploit Symmetry

  • Invariance: Visual systems learn tolerance to translation/rotation/scale (object constancy).
  • Equivariance: Neural computations preserve group structure (inputs transformed → representations transform predictably).
  • Efficiency: Symmetry reduces data needed; brains & models share parameters across transformed inputs.
